discovery: The optical lattice clock: magic-wavelength trapping of neutral atoms enabling optical frequency standards at the 10^-18 level

nominees.name: Hidetoshi Katori
nominees.affiliation: University of Tokyo and RIKEN, Japan

nominees.name: Jun Ye
nominees.affiliation: JILA, NIST and University of Colorado Boulder, USA

subfield: Atomic physics / precision measurement and optical metrology
motivation: Katori proposed and demonstrated that neutral atoms confined in an optical lattice at a 'magic' wavelength experience no differential light shift, breaking with the dogma that trapping necessarily perturbs the clock transition. This allowed thousands of atoms to be interrogated at once without Doppler and recoil effects. Ye transformed the concept into the most accurate and stable clocks ever built, using ultrastable lasers, frequency combs and control of many-body interactions, reaching fractional uncertainties near 10^-18 and resolving the gravitational redshift across a millimetre-scale atomic sample. Optical lattice clocks now underpin the planned redefinition of the SI second, enable relativistic geodesy, and provide sensitive searches for variations of fundamental constants and dark matter. This is a discovery that built on the 2005 frequency-comb Prize and completes it: it turns quantum control of atoms into the most precise measurement in all of physics.
